extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament and the politically engaged public (late-18th-century Britain)
extracted.subtask_description: A parliamentary political address arguing against governmental corruption and maladministration in India, exposing abuses and proposing principles of prudence and justice for handling pecuniary and territorial settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles to avoid suspicion in pecuniary settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: The way to avoid suspicion in the settlement of pecuniary transactions is to: (1) hear all parties equally, not only the managers for the suspected claimants; (2) not proceed in the dark, but act with as much publicity as possible; (3) not to precipitate decision; (4) be religious in following the rules prescribed in the commission under which we act; and (5) above all, not to be fond of straining constructions, forcing a jurisdiction, or drawing to ourselves the management of an invidious trust where the plainest letter of the law does not compel it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these rules are observed, no corruption ought to be suspected; violation of any of them increases suspicion in proportion, and violation of all warrants presuming corrupt motive. The list functions as procedural safeguards—hear all sides, ensure publicity, avoid haste, follow the commission's rules, and respect plain legal limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep subsistence resources independent of political arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Means of subsistence (exemplified by the river Cavery and water use) ought never to be connected with political arrangements, or made to depend on the personal conduct of princes; benefits necessary for a community's subsistence should be as immutable as the laws of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of essential natural resources should not be conditioned on payments, tributes, or political bargains; making food/water contingent on political payments risks famine and long-term ruin for millions. Management of such resources must ensure reproduction of revenues and be insulated from transient political disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribute requires real sovereign power (legitimacy tied to protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribute 'hangs on the sword'—it is inseparable from real sovereign power. To exact tribute without the corresponding military/protective capacity (i.e., when the supposed potentate is deprived of war or peace powers and cannot protect the people) is absurd, cruel, and oppressive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposing tribute where no genuine protection or sovereignty exists is illegitimate; tribute must be linked to actual sovereign obligations and capacities, not retained as a fiction to serve extortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presume collusion when authorities act on concealed real interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever those in authority provide for the interest of any person on the real but concealed state of his affairs (rather than his ostensible pretences), it must be presumed that they are in confederacy with him, because they act for him on the same fraudulent principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of authorities rewarding individuals despite contrary public testimony or known concealment (e.g., reinstating a debtor despite documentary renunciations) indicates collusion. Such inferences rest on the combination and comparison of surrounding circumstances rather than isolated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting clandestine and collusive practice requires circumstantial synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Clandestine and collusive practices can only be traced by combination and comparison of circumstances; rejecting such a method is to reject the only means of detecting fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should assemble and compare chains of facts and relationships (appointments, electoral management, transfers of debt, contradictory testimonies) to reveal patterns of corruption; piecemeal dismissal of circumstantial evidence enables impunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active correction and oversight required for abuses of remote delegated power
rubrics_metrics.description: Abuses of remote, delegated power (especially when productive of unmeasured wealth and protected by ill-got riches) will flourish under mere neglect; even wise government finds it difficult to correct them without active attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous oversight and vigorous corrective measures are necessary to check systemic abuses arising from distant administration and concentrated wealth; neglect allows abuses to grow and embed themselves.
